title: Geo-validated compliance briefing shipments (PDF/CSV) with automated manifests
creator: Sofia Martinez
description:
Scope: Implement a tenant-configurable scheduled ‘compliance briefing’ pipeline that produces PDF and CSV delivery artifacts plus a signed geo-validated manifest per delivery. The pipeline must enforce tenant data residency and retention policies, include a cryptographically-signed manifest for provenance, and provide per-delivery telemetry for observability.

Goals:
- Allow tenants to configure schedule cadence (daily/weekly/monthly) and formats (PDF, CSV, both).
- Ensure all exported records comply with the tenant's configured residency region and retention window before being included in a package.
- Produce a machine-readable manifest (JSONL/CSV) and a human-readable PDF summary; add a signed manifest (HMAC or KMS-signature) for auditability.
- Deliver artifacts via S3/GCS with region-restricted endpoints or SFTP for on-prem customers; provide retries with exponential backoff and SLA metrics.
- Surface delivery status and historic payload metadata in Console dashboards and per-tenant event logs.

Acceptance criteria:
- Config UI or API to schedule briefings and select formats and retention snapshot date (Console + API).
- Export job respects residency tags on records and excludes records outside residency/retention rules.
- Generated manifest includes counts, SHA256 checksums for each file, signed assertion of residency and retention policy used.
- Delivery attempts recorded; final status (delivered/failed/retried) visible in Console and telemetry ingestion.
- End-to-end e2e test covering tenant with EU residency using dedicated S3 endpoint.

Out of scope:
- Deep content redaction (PII removal) — handled by separate redaction pipeline.

Constraints and trade-offs:
- We will use server-side streaming for CSV generation to avoid memory spikes; PDFs will be generated from cached summary snapshots to control runtime CPU.
- For signing manifests we prefer KMS-backed signatures (HSM where available) for strong auditability; fallback to HMAC when key-managed options are unavailable.
- Choosing region-specific object storage endpoints adds operational complexity but is required for strict residency customers.

Success metrics:
- 99% of scheduled briefings complete within SLA window for non-burst tenants.
- Manifest signature verification passes in 100% of audited samples.
- Reduction in manual compliance ticket volume by 60% for participating tenants.

2025-02-24 Priya Nair (Eng): Design review: prefer KMS-based manifest signing. Noted performance hit for on-the-fly PDF renders; propose cached daily summaries and incremental CSV deltas for large tenants. Action: spike for PDF caching (ENG-32411).

2025-02-26 Helena Cho (Design): UX mockups added to Confluence. Console will expose schedule, last-run summary, and per-file checksums. Link: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/COMPLIANCE/Briefing+Shipments+Flow

2025-02-28 Security review request submitted. Raised question about long-term signature verification for exported manifests; security recommends embedding signer identity and KMS key version in manifest. Ticket assigned to SecOps for review.

2025-03-03 Arjun Patel: Implementation plan drafted. Backend: job controller will run at tenant scope, query residency-filtered events, stream CSV to region endpoint, produce PDF via headless renderer from summary template, generate manifest, sign with KMS, and trigger delivery. PR scaffold: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/4832
